close_reason: Added rustdoc warning on ContactCardComparator type and is_ascending field documenting the Default-vs-wire-default semantic divergence. Doc-only, per-crate scope. Commit: 62bd61c.
description:
`ContactCardComparator` derives `Default` (card.rs:463). The resulting
`Default::default()` value has:

  property: ""        (String::default())
  is_ascending: false (bool::default())
  collation: None

Serializing that to JSON emits `{"property":"","isAscending":false}` —
property is required-non-null so it never skips, and is_ascending has
no `skip_serializing_if` so false is emitted explicitly.

But the wire-default for absent `isAscending` is **true** (RFC 8620 §5.5,
encoded by the `#[serde(default = "default_ascending")]` attribute at
card.rs:469-470). Deserializing `{"property":"created"}` produces
`is_ascending: true`, the ascending direction.

So:
  - serialize(Default::default()) → descending sort
  - deserialize(no-isAscending-key) → ascending sort

A caller writing `let mut c = ContactCardComparator::default(); c.property
= "created".into();` then submitting the comparator to a query gets
descending results silently. The Rust API default does not match the
wire-format default semantic — a class of footgun similar to
JMAP-glx8.16 (ContactCard::default() emits wire-invalid {}), but more
dangerous because the result LOOKS valid and just returns the wrong
result set.

The canonical extension-types comparator EmailComparator
(jmap-mail-types/src/query.rs:301-321) solves this by:
  - NOT deriving Default.
  - Providing `EmailComparator::new(property)` that sets `is_ascending: true`.
  - Documenting "Use EmailComparator::new to construct from outside this crate".

The 3-sibling consensus (CalendarEventComparator, TaskComparator,
TaskNotificationComparator) derives Default and shares the same gap.
JMAP-glx8.4 closed by aligning ContactCardComparator to the 3-sibling
Default-deriving consensus per workspace canonical-template policy.
JMAP-glx8.6 / JMAP-18qe track the workspace-API skip_serializing_if
sweep (a different facet — wire-emit-vs-skip, not Default-vs-wire-default).

Neither bead addresses the Default-vs-wire-default semantic gap. This
finding is a per-crate documentation request: add a one-paragraph
warning on the ContactCardComparator type or on the is_ascending field
explaining that Default::default().is_ascending is false but the
wire-default for absent isAscending is true, and recommending callers
either set is_ascending explicitly or construct a typed factory.

The canonical-template-vs-Default-derive question (should all 4
extension-types siblings drop Default in favor of ::new(property),
matching EmailComparator?) is workspace-wide scope and properly belongs
on a new workspace-API sweep bead (sibling of JMAP-18qe), not this
per-crate review. Filing here only as a doc-gap finding to keep the
per-crate review honest.

Suggested rustdoc (on the type, just above the existing "Excluded from
extras preservation" section, or on the is_ascending field):

```
# Default impl divergence
ContactCardComparator::default() produces is_ascending: false because
of Rust's bool default. The wire-default for absent isAscending is
true (RFC 8620 §5.5). A caller building a comparator via Default and
mutating only `property` gets DESCENDING sort silently. Set
is_ascending explicitly when constructing.
```

Scope: card.rs only. No code change required. Workspace-canonical
pattern preserved.
title: ContactCardComparator::default() produces is_ascending=false, diverging from wire-default true for absent isAscending
